root_cause.text: In the netfs subsystem, `netfs_read_unlock_folios()` incorrectly limits the end check of a folio (`fend`) to the file size (`rreq->i_size`) instead of the actual folio boundary, causing the folio to be unlocked prematurely before a subsequent ZERO subrequest can clear the remaining tail of the folio.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that `fend` in `netfs_read_unlock_folios()` is changed from `umin(fpos + fsize, rreq->i_size)` to `fpos + fsize`, ensuring that the end check always aligns with the end of the folio rather than the end of the file.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `netfs_read_unlock_folios` is introduced in this commit. It contains the vulnerable statement `fend = umin(fpos + fsize, rreq->i_size);` which incorrectly limits the end check of the folio (`fend`) to the file size (`rreq->i_size`) instead of the actual folio boundary (`fpos + fsize`). This allows the folio to be unlocked prematurely once `collected_to` reaches `rreq->i_size`, before a subsequent ZERO subrequest can clear the remaining tail of the folio.
